reasoning: Recent publicly-available data focus almost entirely on the 2026 Democratic Senate primary rather than general-election matchups, and one aggregate site offers a synthesized general-election margin that is still based on June polling for Massachusetts voters. Across those sources, Ed Markey holds a dominant advantage both in the primary (roughly D+28 vs Moulton) and in the general-election polling average (about D+23 vs Republican John Deaton), so the effective current margin for the Senate race in Massachusetts is solidly D+. Because there are no fresh, state-level presidential general-election polls in the last 45 days in the results, I treat the presidential state margin as unspecified here and rely only on structural data (Massachusetts’s D+14 Cook PVI) to underscore its Democratic lean.

sources.name: Pollsmax
sources.details: Pollsmax’s 2026 Massachusetts Senate polling average, aggregating seven state-level general-election polls including a June 23 UNH Survey Center poll, shows Ed Markey at 54.1% and Republican John Deaton at 31.0%, a D+23.1 margin.
sources.date_range: up to August 17, 2026 (aggregate of polls, latest fieldwork June 23, 2026)

sources.name: UMass Amherst/WCVB via GBH
sources.details: A UMass Amherst/WCVB poll of 445 Democratic primary voters finds Ed Markey leading Seth Moulton 60% to 32% in the Massachusetts U.S. Senate Democratic primary, a D+28 primary margin.

sources.name: Boston Herald (UMass Amherst/WCVB poll)
sources.details: Reporting on the same UMass Amherst/WCVB poll notes Markey at 60% and Moulton at 32% among Democratic and independent primary voters, reinforcing a roughly D+28 primary lead in the Senate race context.

sources.name: Boston.com (UMass Amherst/WCVB poll)
sources.details: Boston.com’s coverage of the UMass Amherst/WCVB survey likewise describes Markey with 60% support versus Moulton’s 32% among Democratic primary voters, indicating a double-digit, roughly D+28 primary advantage.

sources.name: PredictionHunt (UNH Survey Center primary poll)
sources.details: A UNH Survey Center Democratic primary poll cited by PredictionHunt shows Markey at 41% and Moulton at 35% among likely Democratic primary voters, a D+6 primary margin at that earlier point in the campaign.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Survey Center (via Pollsmax)
sources.details: Within the Pollsmax Massachusetts Senate page, the latest listed general-election poll from the University of New Hampshire fielded June 23 finds Markey leading Deaton 50% to 34%, a D+16 margin among 623 likely voters.

sources.name: Suffolk University (via Pollsmax)
sources.details: Pollsmax also cites a Suffolk University poll from June 12 with Markey at 55% and Deaton at 30% in a Massachusetts Senate general-election matchup, a D+25 margin among 500 registered voters.

sources.name: 270toWin – Latest 2026 Senate Election Polls
sources.details: 270toWin’s latest 2026 Senate election polls page lists Massachusetts among the states with available statewide Senate polling and provides an aggregated view that is consistent with a strong Democratic advantage, though it does not itself specify a single numerical margin for Massachusetts in the last 45 days.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – Cook Partisan Voting Index (Massachusetts statewide)
sources.details: The Cook Partisan Voting Index entry for Massachusetts reports the statewide PVI as D+14, indicating the state voted 14 percentage points more Democratic than the national average in the most recent presidential election and structurally leans strongly Democratic.
sources.date_range: not a poll; index reflects 2020 presidential results

sources.name: Boston Globe (Suffolk University/Boston Globe April primary polling)
sources.details: An April Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll referenced in a July 20 Globe article found Markey winning roughly 40% of voters 35 or younger and nearly 50% of voters aged 36–45 in the Democratic Senate primary, underscoring his demographic strength within the party.
sources.date_range: April 2026 (context, outside strict 45-day window but referenced in late-July story)
